headline: In 1918, Milton Hershey Quietly Put About $60 Million In Stock Into A Trust. Over 100 Years Later, That Trust Still Exists And Holds About $23.6 Billion In Assets. Wealthy Donors Still Use A Similar Strategy, And The Legal Work To Set One Up Starts At A Few Thousand Dollars
summary: A childless candy maker secretly handed his fortune to orphans in 1918, and the legal structure he chose still controls one of America's biggest snack companies today. Wealthy donors quietly use a version of the same playbook, but the fine print carries some serious surprises.

headline: Should Tyson Foods Stock Holders Look At JM Smucker Instead?
summary: Tyson Foods (TSN) and JM Smucker (SJM) both sell grocery brands that shoppers buy every week, from Hillshire Farm and Jimmy Dean to Uncrustables and Milk-Bone. Beyond those familiar labels, the two companies part ways. Tyson runs chicken, beef and pork businesses, while Smucker sells coffee and peanut butter. Over the past year, investors have favored Smucker, whose stock returned 28.0% against 6.2% for Tyson. So is Smucker's outlook improving while Tyson's slips.
